name: Andorra
summary: Possessing drugs for own use is a crime (prison up to 1 year or arrest, plus fine); cannabis is a minor offence (arrest or fine). A new Penal Code (Llei 18/2026) raises the fines from mid-December 2026.
poisonControlNote: No national poison centre found; call SUM 116. Spain's SIT (+34 91 562 04 20, 24h) is the nearest Spanish-language centre.
callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan law. Own-use possession is a crime, so police involvement is possible. Failing to help or call for help for someone in grave danger is an offence.

lsd.note: Own-use possession is a crime: prison up to 1 year or arrest, plus fine up to €1,200 (2 years in public venues). New Code from mid-Dec 2026: fine €1,000–2,000.

mushrooms.note: Psilocybin is internationally controlled, so it counts as a 'toxic drug': own-use possession is a crime (prison up to 1 year or arrest, plus fine).

dmt.note: Own-use possession is a crime: prison up to 1 year or arrest, plus fine up to €1,200 (2 years in public venues). New Code from mid-Dec 2026: fine €1,000–2,000.

nbomes.note: Own-use possession is a crime: prison up to 1 year or arrest, plus fine up to €1,200 (2 years in public venues). New Code from mid-Dec 2026: fine €1,000–2,000.

2c-x.note: Own-use possession is a crime: prison up to 1 year or arrest, plus fine up to €1,200 (2 years in public venues). New Code from mid-Dec 2026: fine €1,000–2,000.

2c-t-x.note: Not UN-scheduled, but the Penal Code also covers substances of 'similar nature and effects', so likely treated as a toxic drug (own-use possession is a crime).

5-meo-xxt.note: Not UN-scheduled, but the Penal Code also covers substances of 'similar nature and effects', so likely treated as a toxic drug (own-use possession is a crime).

cannabis.note: Own-use possession or growing: minor offence, arrest or fine up to €600 (also for public use). From mid-Dec 2026: arrest plus €500–1,200 fine.

ketamine.note: Prescription anaesthetic. Not UN-scheduled, but likely a 'toxic drug' under the similarity clause, so non-prescribed possession may be prosecuted.

mxe.note: UN Schedule II since 2016: a 'toxic drug', so own-use possession is a crime (prison up to 1 year or arrest, plus fine).

dxm.note: Not a controlled drug; could not confirm its pharmacy/prescription status in Andorra.

nitrous.note: Not UN-scheduled; no specific rule found.

amphetamines.note: Own-use possession is a crime: prison up to 1 year or arrest, plus fine up to €1,200 (2 years in public venues). New Code from mid-Dec 2026: fine €1,000–2,000.

mdma.note: Own-use possession is a crime: prison up to 1 year or arrest, plus fine up to €1,200 (2 years in public venues). New Code from mid-Dec 2026: fine €1,000–2,000.

cocaine.note: Own-use possession is a crime: prison up to 1 year or arrest, plus fine up to €1,200 (2 years in public venues). New Code from mid-Dec 2026: fine €1,000–2,000.

caffeine.note: Not a controlled substance; sold freely.

alcohol.note: Legal for adults; supplying alcohol to under-18s is an offence (Penal Code 2026, art. 546).

ghb/gbl.note: GHB is UN Schedule II, so own-use possession is a crime; GBL/1,4-BD may fall under the 'similar effects' clause.

opioids.note: Heroin: own-use possession is a crime (prison up to 1 year or arrest, plus fine). Prescription opioids are medical-only.

benzodiazepines.note: Prescription-only; UN Schedule IV, so non-prescribed possession could be prosecuted as own-use drug possession.

maois.note: MAOI antidepressants are prescription-only; status of harmala alkaloids/ayahuasca not confirmed.
